name: Pasta alla Norma
steps: Check that the rigatoni contains eggless and the cheese label confirms vegetarian coagulants. Cut the eggplant into 2 cm cubes, leaving the purple skin on. Chop the tomatoes, mince the garlic and tear the basil leaves. Pat the eggplant dry so it browns instead of steaming.

Heat 45 ml olive oil in a large wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook the eggplant in two batches for 8–10 minutes each, turning occasionally, until golden with soft centres and some browned edges. Do not crowd the pan. Transfer to a plate and sprinkle with 2 g salt.

Lower the heat to medium and add 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Cook garlic for 30 seconds without browning. Add chopped tomatoes, 4 g salt and black pepper. Simmer uncovered for 12–15 minutes, stirring and pressing the tomatoes, until thick and no longer raw-tasting. Fold two-thirds of the browned eggplant and most basil into the sauce; keep the best pieces and a few leaves for topping.

Meanwhile boil 2400 ml water with 8 g salt. Cook rigatoni according to the packet until just al dente. Reserve 150 ml cloudy pasta water and drain the pasta. Add rigatoni to the tomato-eggplant sauce with 60–100 ml reserved water; toss over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until every tube is coated, adding more water only if dry.

Divide among four warm bowls. Top evenly with the reserved golden eggplant, grated vegetarian ricotta salata-style cheese, remaining basil and final 5 ml olive oil. Serve immediately while the eggplant is tender and the sauce clings to the pasta.
tips: The reviewed image shows ridged short pasta, prominently browned eggplant, bright tomato, basil and a small amount of white cheese. Browning the eggplant in batches is essential. Use only cheese confirmed free of animal rennet; ordinary hard grating cheese is not automatically vegetarian.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
